Call For Applications: Commonwealth Startup Fellowship 2026/2027(Fully Funded To Bootcamp In Accra, Ghana And Capstone Week In London, UK )
Applications are now open for the 2026/2027 Commonwealth Startup Fellowship, a six-month program designed to help high-potential startups from low and middle-income Commonwealth countries scale their businesses, attract investment and create jobs.
Delivered by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) in partnership with Imperial College London, the fellowship combines immersive in-person experiences with online learning to equip founders with advanced entrepreneurial skills, global networks and practical strategies for business growth.
By the end of the programme, participants are expected to strengthen their ability to scale their ventures, pitch confidently to investors and expand their economic impact in their home countries.
The fellowship includes a two-week bootcamp in Accra, Ghana, and a week-long Capstone Week in London, United Kingdom. One representative from each selected startup must attend both in-person events.
Eligibility Criteria
To qualify, applicants must:
- Be at least graduate level.
- Be a citizen of, or have refugee status in, an eligible low or middle-income Commonwealth country.
- Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country.
- Be fluent in written and spoken English.
- Not have undertaken a Commonwealth Professional Fellowship within the last five years.
- Be available to begin the fellowship on 16 November 2026.
- Be available to attend the Bootcamp in Accra, Ghana (estimated 25 January – 4 February 2027).
- Be available to attend the Capstone Week in London, UK (estimated 14 – 21 May 2027).
Applicants must also have a startup that:
- Is legally registered in accordance with local regulations.
- Demonstrates innovation through its product, service, business model or approach to solving a market need.
- Has progressed beyond the idea, prototype and pilot stages.
- Has been operating actively for at least 12 months with measurable progress.
- Offers a product or service already available to customers.
- Can demonstrate customer demand through paying customers and continued adoption, such as repeat purchases, recurring revenue or contract renewals.
- Operates on a sustainable business model rather than relying primarily on grants or donations.
- Creates positive economic, social or environmental impact.
- Shows evidence of commercial traction, growth and strong scaling potential.
- Is seeking to expand its customer base, operations, impact or geographic reach.
Eligible Countries
The fellowship is open to applicants from the following Commonwealth countries:
Bangladesh, Belize, Botswana, Cameroon, Dominica, Eswatini, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Montserrat, Mozambique, Namibia, Nauru, Nigeria, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, St Helena, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu and Zambia.
Fellowship Benefits
Successful applicants will receive:
- Return airfare, accommodation, local travel and meals for the bootcamp in Accra, Ghana.
- Return airfare, accommodation, local travel and meals for the Capstone Week in London, United Kingdom.
- Reimbursement of standard visa application fees.
- An equity-free grant of up to £2,000 to support business or participation-related costs.
- Additional financial support for fellows with disabilities, subject to a needs assessment conducted by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission.
The programme offers founders an opportunity to access world-class entrepreneurship training, mentorship, investor networks and international exposure while accelerating the growth of their businesses.
Interested entrepreneurs can find more details and submit their applications through the official Commonwealth Scholarship Commission website: https://cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk/scholarships/commonwealth-startup-fellowship-information-for-candidates/.

Call for Applications: Chevening UK Government Scholarships 2027 (Fully Funded)
Applications are now open for the 2027 Chevening Scholarships, the UK Government’s flagship fully funded scholarship program for outstanding emerging leaders worldwide.
Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and partner organizations, the scholarship enables exceptional professionals to pursue a one-year master’s degree at any eligible UK university, while building leadership skills, expanding global networks, and gaining international experience.
Eligibility Criteria
Applicants must:
- Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.
- Commit to returning to their home country for at least two years after completing the scholarship.
- Have at least two years (2,800 hours) of post-undergraduate work experience.
- Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies them for admission to a UK master’s program.
- Apply to three eligible UK master’s programs.
- Obtain at least one unconditional offer from a UK university before the Chevening deadline.
Why Apply?
- Chevening offers more than a fully funded education. Scholars will:
- Study at leading UK universities.
- Develop leadership and professional skills.
- Build lifelong international networks.
- Experience UK culture.
- Join a global alumni community of influential leaders across government, business, academia, media, and civil society.
Scholarship Benefits
Successful applicants will receive:
- Full tuition fees
- Monthly living allowance (stipend)
- Economy return airfare to and from the UK
- Arrival and departure allowances
- UK visa application fee
- Travel allowance
- Contribution towards TB testing (where required)
- Access to exclusive networking, leadership, and professional development events
- Membership of the prestigious global Chevening Alumni Network
Application Timeline
- Applications Open: 4 August 2026 (11:00 UTC)
- Application Deadline: 6 October 2026 (11:00 UTC)
- Eligibility Screening: October 2026
- Application Assessment: October 2026 – January 2027
- Interview Shortlist: Mid-February 2027
- Interviews: March – April 2027
- Results Released: Mid-June 2027
- University Offer Deadline: 8 July 2027
- Studies Begin: September/October 2027

Applications open for the Pave Her Way Women’s Grant Programs, a global funding initiative designed to empower women through financial support, mentorship, leadership development, and access to a network of change makers.
The program supports women at different stages of their personal and professional journeys, whether they are established leaders creating impact, innovators developing transformative ideas, or women seeking financial assistance to advance their education or careers.
Who Should Apply?
The programme is open to women who:
- Have demonstrated leadership in their communities or professions
- Are developing innovative projects benefiting women and girls
- Need financial support for education or career advancement
- Face financial barriers to achieving their goals
- Want to scale their impact and expand their leadership
- Are committed to empowering women and creating positive social change
Applicants from all sectors are encouraged to apply, including education, healthcare, business, technology, science, journalism, social entrepreneurship, arts, environmental conservation, government, and community development.
Funding Opportunities
1. Change Agent Prize
This award recognizes accomplished women who have demonstrated exceptional leadership and measurable impact in improving the lives of women and girls.
Funding:
- Up to $90,000
Additional Benefits:
- Optional mentorship
- Cohort learning experience
- Networking opportunities
- Access to a global community of women leaders

The Disruptor Award supports women with innovative projects or ideas that have the potential to create meaningful change for women and girls.
Projects may focus on:
- Women’s economic empowerment
- Education
- Healthcare
- Technology
- Entrepreneurship
- Leadership development
- Gender equality
- Climate resilience
- Financial inclusion

FG Empowers 100 Women, Youths with Livestock Assets to Grow Businesses, Boost Food Production
The Federal Ministry of Livestock Development has empowered 100 women and youths with livestock and production inputs to help them start or expand businesses, improve household incomes and contribute to food production.
The beneficiaries, comprising 52 women and 48 youths, received 100 bullocks, heifers and other livestock production inputs at an empowerment programme held in Dutse, Jigawa State.
The initiative, which brought together beneficiaries from the North-West, North-East and North-Central geopolitical zones, was implemented by the ministry in collaboration with Meteorite Logistics Ltd.
Speaking at the event, Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Maiha, represented by the Director of Livestock Extension and Business Development, said the programme reflects the Federal Government’s efforts to transform the livestock sector while creating jobs and sustainable livelihoods.
He said providing women and young people with quality breeding stock and productive livestock assets would help them participate more actively in the livestock value chain.
According to the minister, the intervention is expected to improve livestock productivity, increase household incomes, promote entrepreneurship and create sustainable economic opportunities, particularly in rural communities.
He urged beneficiaries to properly manage the animals, adopt improved animal husbandry practices and expand their herds to maximise the long-term benefits of the support.
Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Dr Maryam Miko, Jigawa State Coordinator of the Association of Women in Agriculture and Rural Farmers of Nigeria (AWARFAN), said the support would help her establish a livestock business, increase her family’s income and contribute to food production.
Umar Usman, who received the items on behalf of his wife, Hannatu Musa, also commended the government for supporting women and vulnerable households, saying the intervention would strengthen their household income and food security.
Jigawa State representative of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Ahmed Abubakar, said the intervention would help livestock farmers improve production and strengthen the state’s livestock economy.
